document_title: Low Power Double Data Rate 5 (LPDDR5) SDRAM Standard
version: JESD209-5 (original), with addenda JESD209-5B (LPDDR5/5X) and JESD209-5X (LPDDR5X)
manufacturer: JEDEC Solid State Technology Association (multi-vendor consortium standard)
publisher: JEDEC Solid State Technology Association, 3103 North 10th Street, Suite 240 South, Arlington, VA 22201-2107
copyright: Copyright JEDEC Solid State Technology Association 2019
abstract: LPDDR5 (Low Power Double Data Rate 5) SDRAM is a high-speed, low-power, mobile dynamic random-access memory standardized by JEDEC as JESD209-5. LPDDR5 introduces a new clocking architecture that uses a quarter-speed master clock (CK) for command/address together with a full-speed Write Clock (WCK) and Read Strobe (RDQS) which are enabled only when needed, achieving a data transfer rate of up to 6400 Mbit/s per pin. The number of banks is increased to 16, divided into four DDR4-style bank groups, while the prefetch remains 16n (not doubled relative to LPDDR4). LPDDR5 narrows the command/address (CA) bus to 7 bits transferred at double data rate, reduces VDDQ to 0.5 V, and adds power-saving features including dynamic voltage/frequency scaling, Data-Copy / Write-X commands, deep sleep, and Read/Write Link ECC. Low-power state entry is performed by a command over the CA bus that lasts until the chip select signal next goes high, eliminating the Clock Enable (CKE) pin used in LPDDR4.
external_pins: CK_t, CK_c (differential quarter-speed master clock input; command/address timing reference)
WCK_t, WCK_c (differential full-speed Write Clock input; enabled only when needed; 4x the CK rate)
RDQS_t, RDQS_c (differential full-speed Read Strobe; DRAM-driven during reads; enabled only when needed)
CS (chip select; active-high; low-power-mode duration governed by CS)
DQ (bidirectional data bus; x16 per channel, organized as two x8 byte groups)
DMI (Data Mask / Data Bus Inversion, per byte group)
ZQ (calibration reference pin; external precision resistor)
VDD1 (first core supply, ~1.8 V; charge-pump / wordline domain)
VDD2H / VDD2L (second core / periphery supplies; DVFSC selects high/low)
VDDQ (DQ / IO supply, reduced to 0.5 V)
external_pin_count_x16_single_channel_su: Per x16 channel: CK pair (2), WCK pair (2), RDQS pair (2), CA[6:0] (7), CS (1), DQ (16), DMI (2 per byte group), RESET_n shared, ZQ shared, plus VDD1 / VDD2H / VDD2L / VDDQ / VSS / VSSQ power rails. Exact ballout per JESD209-5 package tables.
key_features: 16-bank internal architecture divided into four bank groups (DDR4-style BG0..BG3, each with 4 banks) — selectable bank-group mode (BG mode) or 16-bank mode.
16n prefetch architecture (prefetch is NOT doubled relative to LPDDR4 but remains 16n).

New clocking architecture: quarter-speed differential master clock CK for command/address + full-speed differential Write Clock WCK + full-speed differential Read Strobe RDQS, where WCK and RDQS are enabled only when a transfer is imminent.

WCK-to-CK synchronization (WCK2CK sync) commands — WS_FS (free-start), WS_RD (read-optimized), WS_WR (write-optimized) — issued via the Column Address Select (CAS) command to prepare the DRAM for the high-speed WCK clock before a read/write.
One set of full-speed WCK clocks per byte (vs per 16 bits in LPDDR4).
Data transfer rate up to 6400 Mbit/s per pin (LPDDR5); JESD209-5B/5X (LPDDR5X) extends speed up to 8533 Mbit/s.
7-bit double-data-rate command/address (CA) bus — narrower than DDR but transferred at DDR so commands arrive at the same time as LPDDR4.
Elimination of the Clock Enable (CKE) pin — low-power mode is entered by a command over the CA bus and lasts until the chip select (CS) signal next goes high.
Reduced VDDQ to 0.5 V for lower IO power.
Read Link ECC and Write Link ECC for on-the-wire single-bit error correction (16-bit link ECC).
Data Bus Inversion (DBI) on the DMI lines to minimize the number of bits driven during transfers (power + SI).
Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) including Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling Core (DVFSC) selecting VDD2H / VDD2L.
Decision Feedback Equalization (DFE) on the receiver for signal integrity at 6400 Mbps.
Data-Copy and Write-X (all-zero / all-one) commands to decrease data-transfer activity and save power.
Multi-bank refresh modes: all-bank refresh (REFab) and per-bank refresh (REFpb, round-robin bank address).
Deep sleep mode (DSM) for lowest standby power.
Burst length 16 (BL16) and double-length burst 32 (BL32); reads may specify a starting position within the 32-word aligned burst.
Two-deck architecture (deck mode) splitting the device into two decks for finer power / access granularity.
CA bus DDR encoding (commands span two CA transfers, rising + falling clock, per the LPDDR5 command encoding table).
topology_summary: Source-synchronous low-power mobile memory bus. An LPDDR5 memory controller (master) drives the quarter-speed differential CK, the 7-bit DDR CA bus, CS, and (when a transfer is imminent) the full-speed differential Write Clock WCK to one or more LPDDR5 SDRAM devices (slaves) per channel. DQ and DMI are bidirectional; RDQS (Read Strobe) is driven by the DRAM during reads. Unlike DDR3, there is no CKE pin — power-down/low-power entry is a CA-bus command bounded by CS. Devices commonly use a two-channel (x16 per channel) package and a two-deck internal organization.
density_organization_summary: LPDDR5 dies are organized per x16 channel with 16 banks (four bank groups of four banks) in BG mode, or 16 banks flat in 16B mode, or 8 banks in 8B mode for some densities. Mobile densities range across 2 Gb..32 Gb dies, packaged as multi-die PoP / discrete packages of up to tens of GB total. Exact density/organization tables are defined in JESD209-5.

revision_history.description: Initial LPDDR5 SDRAM Standard release by JEDEC JC-42.6 (Low Power Memory). Introduces WCK/RDQS clocking, 16-bank/4-bank-group architecture, 6400 Mbps, 7-bit DDR CA bus, link ECC, DVFS, deep sleep, CKE elimination.
LPDDR5/5X update: speed extension up to 8533 Mbit/s, signal-integrity improvements with tx/rx equalization, reliability improvements via the new Adaptive Refresh Management feature.
LPDDR5X branded extension reaching 8533+ Mbit/s; later Samsung/Micron/SK Hynix devices (LPDDR5X-8533, LPDDR5T-9600, LPDDR5X-10700) push speeds higher on 14/12 nm-class processes.

use_cases: Main memory in smartphones, tablets, and ultra-mobile / battery-powered devices where power per bit is critical.
AI / ML mobile accelerators and flagship SoCs (e.g. Snapdragon 888+, Apple M-series, MediaTek Dimensity, Huawei Kirin) requiring high bandwidth at low power.
Automotive infotainment and ADAS compute modules.
Edge-AI and high-bandwidth embedded vision systems.
Package-on-Package (PoP) and discrete LPDDR5 modules on mobile application processors.
overview: LPDDR5 SDRAM is JEDEC's fifth-generation low-power mobile DRAM (JESD209-5). It differs from desktop/server DDR in that it is optimized for low voltage and low power, is usually soldered directly to the device's mainboard, and follows the LPDDR generational naming convention separate from the DDR family. LPDDR5's headline innovation is a new clocking architecture: a quarter-speed master clock (CK) carries command/address on a 7-bit double-data-rate CA bus, while a full-speed Write Clock (WCK) and Read Strobe (RDQS) — enabled only when a transfer is imminent — carry data at up to 6400 Mbit/s per pin. The DRAM is organized as 16 banks in four DDR4-style bank groups; the prefetch remains 16n. To save power, LPDDR5 eliminates the CKE pin (low-power entry is a CA-bus command bounded by CS), reduces VDDQ to 0.5 V, adds Data-Copy / Write-X commands, dynamic voltage/frequency scaling, deep sleep, Read/Write Link ECC, and Data Bus Inversion. The WCK2CK synchronization commands (WS_FS / WS_RD / WS_WR), carried by the CAS command, prepare the DRAM to lock to the imminent high-speed WCK clock before the read or write begins.
